cases.title: Discount-code orders are 3x bigger — blast more codes to grow baskets?
cases.blurb: Promo-code orders average 3x the basket size, and the Head of Growth wants to blast codes to everyone. But who reaches for a code first? Check the margin math before it ships.

cases.title: Enterprise accounts are our most loyal — should we bet the GTM on them?
cases.blurb: Enterprise accounts show the highest retention, so the CRO wants to move upmarket. But the number only counts accounts that survived. Bring back the churned ones.

cases.title: Checklist-completers retain at nearly double — make it mandatory?
cases.blurb: Users who finish onboarding retain at nearly double, and the PM wants to gate the app on it. But who chooses to finish? Estimate the real effect before it ships.

cases.title: Weekly sessions rose after the redesign — did engagement go up?
cases.blurb: Sessions per user rose 12% after the redesign — but it launched with a win-back campaign. Split new vs returning users before calling it a win.

cases.title: SLA breaches jumped after the Airflow 2 migration — roll it back?
cases.blurb: DAGs on Airflow 2 breach SLA 1.6x as often, and the platform lead wants to roll back. But which DAGs were migrated first? Check before the rollback note goes out.

cases.title: Auto-retries pushed task success to 94% — did retries fix reliability?
cases.blurb: Overall task success rose ~2 points after retries went 1→3, and the platform lead calls it the win of the quarter. Split by task class before she presents it.

cases.title: Migrated queries run 60% faster — should we move everything?
cases.blurb: Queries on the new warehouse engine average 60% faster, and the Head of Platform wants to migrate everything. You've got the query logs. Is it the engine — or which queries got moved first?

cases.title: Incidents fell on the tables we validated — did validation work?
cases.blurb: Validation was added to the worst-quality tables and their incidents dropped ~20%. The Head of Data wants it everywhere. Would those tables have improved anyway?

cases.title: Did the win-back email actually lift retention?
cases.blurb: Marketing swears the Q3 win-back email lifted 90-day retention by 30 points. You've got the user-level export. Is the lift real, or is something else going on?

cases.title: Do support tickets cause churn — should we cut the team?
cases.blurb: Accounts that contact support churn far more, so the COO wants to cut the support team to save money and reduce churn. Does the data actually support that?

cases.title: The new checkout converts worse overall — roll it back?
cases.blurb: The redesigned checkout converts lower than the old one overall, and the Head of Growth wants to roll it back. Split the data before she does.

cases.title: Team A's win rate beats Team B — is B underperforming?
cases.blurb: Team A closes 37% of deals, Team B only 30%, and the VP wants to reshuffle B. Compare the pods fairly before anyone gets moved.

cases.title: We coached our worst reps and they improved — does coaching work?
cases.blurb: The worst Q1 reps got coaching and jumped +6.2k while everyone else slipped. Enablement wants to scale it. Is the swing real, or was it always going to happen?

cases.title: We remodeled our worst-rated stores and ratings rebounded — did it work?
cases.blurb: The lowest-rated stores were remodeled and bounced back 5+ points. The VP wants the next tranche. Would those stores have recovered anyway?

cases.title: Users who run 50+ workflows never churn — push everyone to 50?
cases.blurb: Users with 50+ workflows churn at 1% vs 92% for the rest. Product wants '50 workflows' as the North Star. Is it a real lever or a mirage?

cases.title: Referrers are worth 1.8x — should we push referrals to grow LTV?
cases.blurb: Customers who referred a friend have 1.8x the lifetime value. Growth wants a referral push to lift LTV. Does referring make customers valuable — or the other way round?

cases.title: Revenue jumped 64% after the November loyalty launch — did it work?
cases.blurb: Revenue rose 64% right after loyalty launched in November, and the CMO wants to expand it. Two years of orders are in the file. How much is the program vs the holidays?

cases.title: Conversion rose after the December site-speed deploy — did the deploy do it?
cases.blurb: Conversion jumped ~8 points the month a speed improvement shipped — in December. Two years of sessions are in the file. Is it the deploy or the season?

cases.title: K-means found 4 shopper personas — build campaigns around them?
cases.blurb: K-means found 4 shopper personas from visit frequency, session depth, and spend. But one column has a 20x bigger scale than the other two — check what's actually driving the clusters before four campaigns get built.

cases.title: Usage clustering found 5 personas — target onboarding by persona?
cases.blurb: Usage clustering found 5 personas for onboarding — but did it find behavior, or just account size? One unscaled column can decide a whole clustering on its own.

cases.title: The anomaly model flagged 1% as fraud — freeze those accounts?
cases.blurb: An isolation forest flagged the top 1% as fraud. Before anyone auto-freezes an account, check how much of that flag is actually fraud — and who else looks just as unusual.

cases.title: The anomaly detector flagged these hosts as compromised — take them offline?
cases.blurb: The anomaly detector flagged these hosts as compromised. Before quarantine, check how many are just scheduled batch jobs and backups doing their job at 3am.

cases.title: PC1 explains 99.9% of the variance — build the health score on it?
cases.blurb: PC1 explains 99.9% of the variance across four health metrics — sounds like the whole picture in one score. Check whether it actually predicts who churns.

cases.title: PC1 explains 99% of the engagement variance — score users on it?
cases.blurb: PC1 explains 99% of the engagement variance — ready to rank and target users on it. Check whether it predicts who actually comes back.

cases.title: We found 4 stable customer personas — commit next quarter's budget by persona?
cases.blurb: 4 personas came out of one k-means run, and the budget split is about to lock to their sizes. Re-run it and see how many customers land somewhere else.

cases.title: Ticket clustering found 4 issue types — route tickets by cluster ID?
cases.blurb: Ticket clustering found 4 issue types, and support-ops wants to route by cluster ID. Re-run the same clustering and see how many tickets change queues.

cases.title: Clustering discovered a high-value segment — target it for upsell?
cases.blurb: Clustering "discovered" a high-value segment worth a new upsell motion. Check whether it's just the enterprise tier wearing a data-science label.

cases.title: Clustering revealed a high-risk churn group — target it with an intervention?
cases.blurb: Clustering revealed a "new" at-risk group worth its own re-engagement flow. Check whether it's just account status restated — and where the real signal is hiding.

cases.title: Variant B gets a higher average reward in the logs — roll it out to everyone?
cases.blurb: Variant B's click rate is 20 points higher in the logs — but it was also shown to the most engaged users first. Correct for who actually saw each variant before rolling out.

cases.title: The discount-price arm shows higher revenue per session in the logs — roll it out everywhere?
cases.blurb: The discount arm earns $14 more per session in the logs. Check who actually got shown the discount before believing it — the honest number might have the wrong sign.

cases.title: The CTR bandit lifted clicks 63% — ship it to all traffic?
cases.blurb: A CTR bandit lifted clicks 63%. Check what happened to purchases — the metric the clicks were only ever supposed to lead to.

cases.title: The routing bandit lifted first-touch resolution 41% — roll it out support-wide?
cases.blurb: A routing bandit lifted first-touch resolution 41%. Check the reopen rate before believing those tickets actually got fixed.

cases.title: The learned bidder beats the fixed rule by $2.93/auction — keep it live?
cases.blurb: A learned bidder beats the fixed rule by $2.93/auction averaged over the quarter — but a competitor entered partway through. Split by period before making it permanent.

cases.title: The RL router beats the heuristic by 5.5 points of on-time rate — make it permanent?
cases.blurb: An RL router beats the old heuristic by 5.5 points of on-time rate for the quarter — including the holiday surge. Check whether the edge survives the surge itself.

cases.title: The bandit's average conversion rate beats the old creative — was it worth running?
cases.blurb: A creative bandit's average conversion rate beat the old ad over 40 days. Check the first two weeks separately before calling bandits an automatic win.

cases.title: The subject-line bandit's average open rate beats the old template — was it worth running?
cases.blurb: A subject-line bandit's average open rate beat the old template over 40 days. Check the first two weeks before turning it on for every sequence.

cases.title: The new checkout UI converts better overall — make it the default?
cases.blurb: The new checkout UI converts better overall — but it was also shown to mobile far more than desktop. Split by device before making it the default.

cases.title: The new notification timing gets a higher open rate overall — switch everyone to it?
cases.blurb: The new notification timing gets a higher open rate overall — but weekday-active users saw it far more than weekend users. Split by cohort before switching everyone.
